problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{(x-3)^{n}}{(2n)!}=1+\frac{(x-3)}{2!}+\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{4!}+\frac{(x-3)^{3}}{6!}+⋯\,.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{n}^{2}(2x-6)^{n}=(2x-6)+{2}^{2}(2x-6)^{2}+{3}^{2}(2x-6)^{3}+⋯\,.
$$

$R=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}={n}^{2}(2x-6)^{n}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(n+1)^{2}(2x-6)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}(2x-6)^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(n+1)^{2}(2x-6)}{{n}^{2}}| \\  & =|2x-6|{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{n+1}{n})}^{2} \\  & =|2x-6|\cdot 1 \\  & =|2x-6| \\  & =2|x-3|\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied if $|x-3|<\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\frac{1}{2}.$
